title: Add-on for new game extensions
description: Describes the add-on whose files sit next to this addon.json. They are generated into src/<id>/ of a new project. The build checks everything here again and fails on a problem.

id.description: The folder's name: a lower-case letter, then letters and digits. The files are generated into src/<id>/.

version.description: A version like 1.0.0. Raise it whenever a file of the add-on changes, then run npm run lock-addons.

name.description: What the wizard shows in its checklist.

description.description: One sentence the wizard shows next to the name.

category.description: Which checklist of the wizard the add-on is in. The categories are in catalogue/categories.json.

engines.description: The engines the add-on is offered for, from catalogue/engines.json. Leave it out to offer it for every engine.

hidden.description: Never shown in the wizard. The add-on only takes part through another add-on's dependsOn, or its own when.

dependsOn.description: Add-ons that are included along with this one.

conflicts.description: Add-ons that can't be picked together with this one. Add-ons for different engines never meet, so they don't need it.

when.description: Included by itself once all of these are picked, for a hidden add-on that makes others work together.

supersedes.description: Add-ons whose hooks, README texts and mods folder this one takes over when both take part. Their register.ts, setup.ts and game.ts aren't generated then.

replacesPlainInstaller.description: The project leaves out the plain installer, which copies the game's mod files into the mods folder (MOD_FILES, INSTALLERS and src/installers/mods.ts).

modsPath.description: Where Vortex deploys mods that no mod type sends elsewhere. At most one add-on of a project may set it.

base.description: game: relative to the game folder. executable: relative to the folder of the game's executable.

path.description: A relative folder, written with /. Use . for the base folder itself.

hooks.description: The functions the generated project calls.

register.description: A function register.ts exports. main() calls it with the extension context: name(context).

setup.description: A function setup.ts exports. prepareForModding awaits it: await name(discovery, api).

game.description: A function game.ts exports, typed (context: types.IExtensionContext) => Pick<types.IGame, ...>. main() spreads what it returns into registerGame.

fields.description: Every registerGame field the function returns. The baseline's own fields are taken, and two add-ons that can be picked together can't both return one.

options.description: Questions the wizard asks once the add-ons are picked. A template uses an option's value as {{optionId}}.

readme.description: Bullets for the generated README. They may use {{gameName}} and the option placeholders. A section of its own goes into addon.md.

features.description: Bullets for the list of what the extension does.

notes.description: Bullets for what the author should check before releasing.

projectFiles.description: Files of the add-on's folder that go elsewhere in the project, such as a GitHub workflow: the file's path in the folder, then its path in the project. Not for TypeScript, which stays in src/<id>/.

packageJson.description: What the add-on adds to the generated package.json. The baseline's own entries are taken.

devDependencies.description: Packages the add-on needs to build. Libraries Vortex provides go into vortexLibraries.

scripts.description: npm scripts, added after the baseline's.

vortexLibraries.description: Libraries Vortex provides at runtime that the add-on imports. Each is added to devDependencies, so it type-checks, and to "vortex": { "externals" }, so rollup leaves it to Vortex.

gitignore.description: Lines appended to the generated .gitignore, below the add-on's name.

placeholder.description: The hint in the question's input box.

choices.description: The answers. The first one is the default.

detail.description: A line the wizard shows below the label.

placeholders.description: Text that differs between the choices, used as {{name}} in addon.md and the readme bullets. Every choice defines the same names.
